title: Father's work: furs, then a gambling place on Davis Avenue
summary: His father bought furs from country trappers, then opened a successful gambling place on Mobile's main street, forbidding Cootie to go near it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I see. I see. And, well, what did your father do in Mobile, Cootie?
Well, he did sort of a lot of different things. First he worked for a furrier. He used to go to the
What kind of furs?
Whatever they killed.
I mean, what would there be there? Muskrat or would there be mink, or --
I don't recall.
You don't recall.
Right now. But I know that's what he did.
I suppose people on the farms trapped them or something.
Yeah.
Yeah.
And he used to go out in the country and buy these furs from these people.
I see.
Give them little or nothing for them.
Yes.
(Laughter)
And eventually he and another fellow opened up a gambling place there in Mobile.
Tell me about that. What was it like?
Well --
I mean, was it on the main street?
Yes, it was on the main street.
I see.
Davis Avenue.
Yeah.
We called it the Street there. And -- of course, I wasn't allowed in there.
No.
I didn't ever get to look at it. I knew where it was situated, but he didn't allow me in the pool room.
There was a pool room?
No. It wasn't -- he didn't own the pool room.
Oh.
But he didn't allow me to go into the pool room.
No. No. Well, Cootie, what did they do, shoot craps and --
I don't know what all they did.
-- play blackjack. You don't know.
I don't know what he had in the gambling place.
But he did all right.
Oh, yeah.
I mean he did this for a long time?
Yeah. He was very successful at it.
Oh, well that was good, then. So you come by it legitimately, Cootie.
(Laughter)
